In this C++ repository (D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs), there's a bug where audit log messages are being formatted identically to standard/regular log entries instead of using a specialized audit formatter that includes user_id and ip fields.

Please investigate and report back:
1. Find the logging classes/hierarchy (e.g., LogEntry, LogMessage, or similar base classes, and any AuditLog / AuditEntry subclass or variant).
2. Find the formatter/serialization classes (e.g., LogFormatter, Serializer, or similar) — especially any specialized "audit formatter" class that knows about user_id/ip fields.
3. Find the code path where a log message gets dispatched/routed to a formatter — e.g. a factory function, a switch/if-chain on log type, a virtual method, RTTI check (dynamic_cast, typeid), or use of the base class type instead of derived type causing slicing or wrong dispatch.
4. Identify precisely why the audit-specific formatter is never invoked for audit entries — e.g. wrong type check, missing case in switch, passing by value causing object slicing, storing audit entries in a vector<LogEntry> instead of pointers, incorrect enum/type tag, formatter selected by wrong field, etc.

Report exact file paths and line numbers for all relevant classes/functions, and a precise explanation of the root cause. Do not make any edits — this is research only.

content.text:
## Investigation Report: Audit Log Formatting Bug

### 1. Logging class hierarchy

- **`model::LogMessage`** — base class
  `D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs\src\model\log_message.h:6-14`
  Holds `message_` and exposes `virtual std::string get_text() const`.

- **`model::AuditLogMessage`** — derived class
  `D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs\src\model\audit_log_message.h:6-17`
  Extends `LogMessage`, adding `user_id_` / `ip_address_` with accessors `user_id()` and `ip_address()` (lines 11-12).

### 2. Formatter/serializer classes

- **`serializer::BaseSerializer`**
  `D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs\src\serializer\base_serializer.h:7-18`
  Declares only **one** virtual method:
  ```cpp
  virtual std::string format(const model::LogMessage& msg) { return "[LOG] " + msg.get_text(); }  // line 10-12
  ```
  There is **no** `format(const model::AuditLogMessage&)` declared in the base class. This is already flagged by a comment in the file itself (lines 14-17): *"BUG: Missing virtual declaration of AuditLogMessage formatting overload... to allow derived class overrides to execute when called polymorphically."*

- **`serializer::JsonSerializer`**
  `D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs\src\serializer\json_serializer.h:6-16`
  - Line 8-10: `format(const model::LogMessage& msg) override` — the regular formatter, produces `{"level":"info",...}`.
  - Line 13-15: `format(const model::AuditLogMessage& msg)` — the **audit-specific formatter** that includes `user_id` and `ip`. This is exactly the specialized formatter the bug report refers to, but it is a **plain (non-virtual) overload**, not an override of anything in `BaseSerializer` (there's nothing to override — the base declares no such signature). The file even comments this: *"Overload of format, but cannot override a non-virtual function from base."*

### 3. Dispatch path

- **`logger::AuditLogger`**
  `D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs\src\logger\audit_logger.h:8-21`
  - Line 19: holds a reference typed `serializer::BaseSerializer& serializer_` (not `JsonSerializer&`).
  - Line 12-14:
    ```cpp
    void log(const model::AuditLogMessage& msg) {
        formatted_logs_.push_back(serializer_.format(msg));
    }
    ```
    Calls `serializer_.format(msg)` where `serializer_`'s **static type** is `BaseSerializer&`.

### 4. Root cause

The call `serializer_.format(msg)` is resolved via C++ overload resolution using the **static (compile-time) type of `serializer_`**, which is `BaseSerializer&` — not the runtime type `JsonSerializer`. Overload resolution only considers member functions visible in `BaseSerializer`'s interface, and the only one that exists there is:

```cpp
virtual std::string format(const model::LogMessage& msg)   // base_serializer.h:10
```

Since `AuditLogMessage` derives from `LogMessage`, `msg` implicitly binds to this single overload (reference upcast — no data slicing occurs here, but the audit-specific overload in `JsonSerializer` is completely invisible through the base-typed reference, because it was never declared/declared virtual in `BaseSerializer`). Virtual dispatch then correctly calls `JsonSerializer::format(const LogMessage&)` (json_serializer.h:8-10) — which is the **generic/standard** formatter, not the audit one at json_serializer.h:13-15.

In short, the bug is **not** RTTI misuse or a missing switch/case — it's a classic "overload hiding, not overriding" defect:

- `JsonSerializer::format(const AuditLogMessage&)` (json_serializer.h:13) is a normal (non-virtual) member function overload. It can only be selected by overload resolution against the **static type** of the calling expression.
- Because `BaseSerializer` (the type through which `AuditLogger` always calls `format`) never declares a matching virtual `format(const AuditLogMessage&)` signature, that overload can never participate in the virtual dispatch table and can never be reached polymorphically — regardless of the object's actual runtime type.
- As a result, every `AuditLogMessage` silently falls back to the base `LogMessage` formatting path, producing `{"level":"info",...}` instead of the audit-specific `{"level":"audit",...,"user_id":...,"ip":...}` output — exactly the symptom described (audit entries formatted identically to standard log entries).

**Fix direction (not applied, per instructions):** Add `virtual std::string format(const model::AuditLogMessage& msg)` to `BaseSerializer` (as already noted in its own comment) and mark `JsonSerializer`'s `AuditLogMessage` overload as `override`; alternatively, use a double-dispatch/visitor pattern so the correct formatter is chosen based on the message's runtime type rather than the reference's static type.

### Note on a second, unrelated bug

While investigating, I also noticed a similar-shaped static-binding bug in `dispatcher::MessageDispatcher::route` (`D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-request-bugs\src\dispatcher\message_dispatcher.cpp:12-20`, flagged in-code at line 17-18) where `PriorityMessage` objects passed through a `const Message&`-typed container resolve to the wrong overload. This is a distinct bug from the one you asked about (message routing vs. audit formatting) — flagging it here only for completeness in case it's in scope for a broader fix pass.
